technology_notes: Corrected to match Heart Aerospace ES-30 (the most credible real near-term hybrid-electric program, real airline orders already placed): 30 seats, 200km pure-electric / 800km hybrid range (400km used as a representative mission), real 2031 target entry into service. Was previously modeled at 180 seats (inherited from kerosene_short) with no real program at that scale.

Moved from long-haul to short-haul: hydrogen's poor volumetric energy density makes long-haul the hardest real case, not the easiest (confirmed by the supplied research - no hydrogen option appears for wide-body/very-large aircraft at all). Real anchor: Airbus ZEROe turbofan concept, 120-200 seats, 2,000+ nm range, real 2035 target service entry. Caveat: Airbus itself narrowed focus to the fuel-cell-powered ZEROe variant specifically in 2025, a real signal of even greater timeline uncertainty than the 2035 combustion-concept date alone suggests.

Power-to-liquid e-kerosene (PtL), a real, distinct SAF pathway from HEFA - renewable electricity + captured CO2, not biomass/waste. Drop-in compatible once certified (same aircraft/engine as kerosene, no propulsion hardware change), but real 2026 spot prices run ~2-3x HEFA-SAF (~$5,500/t PtL vs ~$1,800-2,830/t HEFA) - a real operating-cost premium this catalog's capex field does not itself carry (capex reflects aircraft capital cost, not fuel price - the cost gap would need to be modeled at the scenario fuel-price level, not here).

Ultra-high-bypass geared/open-fan engine (CFM RISE program, Safran/GE Aerospace, launched 2021) - real, >20% fuel burn/CO2 reduction vs today's most efficient engines, real 2035 target entry into service. Same fuel compatibility as conventional (Jet A/Jet A-1, certified SAF, e-kerosene) - a more efficient conventional-fuel engine, not an alternative fuel. Capex premium (+8%) is an estimate, not a sourced pre-certification price. Not extended to long-haul: the real program and the supplied research both target the narrow-body/single-aisle replacement market specifically, not wide-body long-haul.
